title: Push Longer? Torque and L Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A kick makes a ball faster. A brake makes a bicycle slower. A force changes momentum. But what changes a spin? When Aarav pushes a merry-go-round for a moment it turns slowly, and when he keeps pushing for longer it spins much faster. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 6, System of Particles and Rotational Motion) we learn how torque and angular momentum are linked.

On a live motion notebook Aarav pushes the rim with 50 N, 1.5 m from the axle, while the readout tracks the torque, the time, L and dL/dt, and a graph shows L climbing in a straight line whose slope is the torque. A slow-mo replay shows r, F and the direction of the torque. Then he lets go, and L stays the same. We prove torque = dL/dt step by step from L = r cross p (why v cross p is zero, and why inside torques cancel for a system), see link by link why a longer push spins it faster, compare force and momentum with torque and angular momentum (angular impulse), and solve a ball on a string example. Then the exam trap (no force vs no torque), an original JEE Main pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.

In this video:
